sentences.zh: 朱克融朱克融，賊泚之從孫也。

translations.literal: Zhu Kerong — Zhu Kerong was the grandnephew of the rebel Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong was a grandnephew of the rebel Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 祖滔，父洄。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Tao; his father was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Zhu Tao, and his father was Zhu Hui.

sentences.zh: 克融少為幽州軍校，事節度使劉總。

translations.literal: Kerong in his youth was a military officer in Youzhou and served the military governor Liu Zong.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Kerong served as a military officer in Youzhou under the military governor Liu Zong.

sentences.zh: 總將歸朝，慮其有變，籍軍中素有異志者，薦之闕下，時克融亦在籍中。

translations.literal: When Zong was about to return to court, fearing there might be trouble, he registered those in the army who had long harbored divergent intentions and recommended them to the capital; at that time Kerong was also on the register.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong prepared to return to court, fearing unrest he drew up a list of men in the army who had long harbored rebellious designs and sent them to the capital; Kerong was among them.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔植、杜元穎不知兵，且無遠略，謂兩河無虞，遂奏勒歸鎮。

translations.literal: The chancellors Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying knew nothing of military affairs and lacked long-range strategy; thinking the Two He regions were secure, they memorialized that the men be ordered back to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying knew nothing of war and had no long-term vision. Assuming the Two He regions were safe, they memorialized that the men be sent back to their garrisons.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，幽州軍亂，囚其帥張弘靖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Changqing reign, the Youzhou army mutinied and imprisoned its commander Zhang Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing era the Youzhou army mutinied and imprisoned their commander Zhang Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 時洄廢疾於家，軍中素伏其謀略，至是眾欲立之。

translations.literal: At that time Hui lay at home with chronic illness; the army had long respected his stratagems, and now the men wished to install him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hui was then confined at home by chronic illness, but the army had long admired his strategic ability, and the troops now wanted to make him their leader.

sentences.zh: 洄自以老且病，推克融統軍務焉。

translations.literal: Hui, considering himself old and ill, yielded command of military affairs to Kerong.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, deeming himself too old and ill to serve, put Kerong in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋加檢校左散騎常侍，授以符節。

translations.literal: The court soon added the acting post of Left Regular Attendant and invested him with seals and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon appointed him acting Left Regular Attendant and invested him with the seals and credentials of office.

sentences.zh: ，遣使送方鎮及三軍時服，克融怒所賜疏弱，執中使以聞。

translations.literal: It dispatched envoys to deliver seasonal clothing for the provincial post and the three armies; Kerong was angered that what was granted was shoddy and detained the imperial envoy to report this.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent envoys with seasonal uniforms for the provincial command and the three armies. Kerong was enraged that the gifts were cheap and inferior, and he detained the imperial envoy to lodge a complaint.

sentences.zh: 上特優容，別命中使宣諭，仍改賜衣物，流其使楊文端等。

translations.literal: The emperor showed special forbearance, separately ordered an imperial envoy to announce and explain, changed the gifts of clothing, and banished the envoys Yang Wenduan and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed unusual forbearance, sent another imperial envoy to explain the matter, replaced the clothing gifts, and banished Yang Wenduan and the other envoys involved.

sentences.zh: 先是，克融執中使，奏稱：「竊聞陛下欲幸東都，請將兵馬並丁匠五千人，修理宮闕，迎候車駕。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Kerong had detained the imperial envoy, he memorialized saying: "I secretly hear that Your Majesty intends to visit the Eastern Capital. I request to bring five thousand troops and laborers to repair the palace halls and welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after detaining the imperial envoy, Kerong memorialized the throne: "I have heard that Your Majesty plans to visit the Eastern Capital. I ask leave to bring five thousand soldiers and craftsmen to repair the palace halls and receive the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 又上言無衣，擬於朝廷請三十萬端疋，以備一歲所費，不然則三軍不安。

translations.literal: He also submitted that they lacked clothing, proposing to request three hundred thousand bolts from the court to cover a year's expenses; otherwise the three armies would not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that his troops lacked clothing and proposed requesting three hundred thousand bolts from the court to cover a year's needs, warning that otherwise the three armies would remain unsettled.

sentences.zh: 天子怒其悖慢，取宰臣裴度謀，優容之，語見別卷。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was angry at his insolence, took counsel with the chancellor Pei Du, and showed forbearance; the account appears in a separate fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious at this insolence, but after consulting Chancellor Pei Du he chose to show forbearance; the full account appears elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 克融官至檢校司空、吳興郡王。

translations.literal: Kerong rose in office to acting Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong eventually reached the posts of acting Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，本州軍亂，殺之，子延齡亦遇害。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month the army of the prefecture mutinied and killed him; his son Yanling also perished.
translations.idiomatic: That May the local army mutinied and killed him; his son Yanling died in the violence as well.

sentences.zh: 次子延嗣竊立，尋為大將李載義所殺。

translations.literal: The second son Yansi seized power in his stead and was soon killed by the great general Li Zaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong's second son Yansi seized power on his own authority, but was soon killed by the general Li Zaiyi.

sentences.zh: 李載義李載義，字方谷，常山湣王之後。

translations.literal: Li Zaiyi — Li Zaiyi, styled Fanggu, was a descendant of the Prince Min of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi, styled Fanggu, was a descendant of the Prince Min of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 代以武力稱，繼為幽州屬郡守。

translations.literal: His family for generations was famed for martial prowess; he succeeded to be prefect of a subordinate commandery in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been known for martial prowess, and he inherited a post as prefect of a Youzhou subordinate commandery.

sentences.zh: 載義少孤，與鄉曲之不令者遊。

translations.literal: Zaiyi was orphaned young and consorted with disreputable locals.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi lost his father while still young and kept company with unruly men of the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 有勇力，善挽強角牴。

translations.literal: He had courage and strength and was skilled at drawing the heavy bow and wrestling.
translations.idiomatic: He was brave and powerful, and excelled at drawing heavy bows and wrestling.

sentences.zh: 劉濟為幽州節度使，見而偉之，致於親軍，從征伐。

translations.literal: When Liu Ji was military governor of Youzhou, he saw him and admired his stature, brought him into his personal guard, and took him on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ji served as military governor of Youzhou, he was struck by Zaiyi's imposing bearing, enrolled him in his personal guard, and took him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 以功遷衙前都知兵馬使，檢校光祿大夫、兼監察御史。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to commander of the vanguard guard, acting Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and concurrently investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to commander of the vanguard guard, with the acting rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and the concurrent post of investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，幽師殺硃克融。

translations.literal: During the Baoli reign, the Youzhou army killed Zhu Kerong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoli era the Youzhou army killed Zhu Kerong.

sentences.zh: 其子延嗣竊襲父位，不遵朝旨，虐用其人；

translations.literal: His son Yansi seized his father's position on his own authority, did not obey court orders, and tyrannized the people.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong's son Yansi seized his father's position without authorization, defied the court's orders, and oppressed the people under his command.

sentences.zh: 載義遂殺之，數其罪以聞。

translations.literal: Zaiyi then killed him and enumerated his crimes in a report.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi then killed him, listed his crimes, and reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嘉之，拜檢校戶部尚書、兼御史大夫，封武威郡王，充幽州盧龍等軍節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong commended him, appointing him acting Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffing him as Prince of Wuwei Commandery, and making him vice military governor of the Youzhou-Lulong armies with charge of military governorship affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong praised his action and appointed him acting Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed him as Prince of Wuwei Commandery, and made him vice military governor of the Youzhou-Lulong circuit with full control of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李同捷據滄景以邀襲父爵。

translations.literal: Before long, Li Tongjie held Cang and Jing to demand succession to his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Tongjie seized Cangzhou and Jingzhou and demanded to inherit his father's title by force.

sentences.zh: 載義上表，請討同捷以自效。

translations.literal: Zaiyi submitted a memorial requesting to campaign against Tongjie to prove his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi memorialized the throne, asking permission to campaign against Tongjie as proof of his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其誠懇，特加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his sincerity and specially added the post of acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased by his earnestness and specially added the acting post of Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 累破賊軍，以功加司空，進階金紫。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated rebel armies; for merit he was made Grand Preceptor and advanced to the Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia rank.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly routed the rebel armies, and for his achievements was promoted to Grand Preceptor and advanced to the rank of Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia.

sentences.zh: ，平滄景，策勛加平章事，仍賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He pacified Cang and Jing; for his recorded merit he was made Grand Counselor and granted three hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Cangzhou and Jingzhou he was made Grand Counselor in recognition of his merit and granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 四年，契丹寇邊，以兵擊走之，仍虜其名王，就加太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Khitan raided the border; he drove them off with troops and captured one of their royal leaders, whereupon he was made Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the Khitan raided the frontier, he drove them off by force and captured one of their royal leaders; he was thereupon promoted to Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 五年春，為其部下楊志誠所逐，因入覲。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifth year he was driven out by his subordinate Yang Zhicheng and therefore came to court for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year his subordinate Yang Zhicheng drove him out, and he came to court to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 上以載義有平滄景之功，又能恭順朝旨，再拜太保、同平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Zaiyi had merit in pacifying Cang and Jing and could respectfully follow court directives, again appointed him Grand Guardian and Concurrent Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zaiyi had pacified Cangzhou and Jingzhou and had shown himself obedient to the court, the emperor again appointed him Grand Guardian and Concurrent Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 其年，改山南西道節度、觀察等使，兼興元尹。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to be military governor and surveillance commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, concurrently governor of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was transferred to military governor and surveillance commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, concurrently serving as governor of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷北都留守，兼太原尹，充河東節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to be defender of the Northern Capital, concurrently governor of Taiyuan, serving as military governor, surveillance commissioner, and disposal commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to defender of the Northern Capital, concurrently governor of Taiyuan and military governor, surveillance commissioner, and disposal commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Grand Preceptor with the same honors as the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further honored as Grand Preceptor with privileges equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復驃騎大將軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: On mourning for his mother he was recalled from mourning as General of Chariots and Cavalry; the rest of his posts remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning, but was recalled from mourning as General of Chariots and Cavalry while retaining his other posts.

sentences.zh: 回鶻每遣使入朝，所至強暴。

translations.literal: Whenever the Uyghurs sent envoys to court, wherever they went they acted violently.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Uyghurs sent envoys to the Tang court, they behaved with violence wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 邊城長吏多務茍安，不敢制之以法。

translations.literal: Frontier officials mostly sought mere safety and did not dare control them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials mostly sought an easy peace and did not dare restrain them by law.

sentences.zh: 但嚴兵防守，虜益驕悍，或突入市肆，暴橫無所憚。

translations.literal: They only posted strict guard troops; the barbarians grew all the more overbearing, sometimes bursting into markets and acting with violent arrogance without fear.
translations.idiomatic: They merely posted heavy guards, which only made the foreigners bolder; some would burst into marketplaces and behave with brazen violence, fearing nothing.

sentences.zh: 至是，有回鶻將軍李暢者，曉習中國事，知不能以法制馭，益驕恣。

translations.literal: At this time there was a Uyghur general named Li Chang who was versed in Chinese affairs and knew they could not be controlled by law, and he grew even more arrogant and willful.
translations.idiomatic: At this time a Uyghur general named Li Chang, who understood Chinese ways, realized that the frontier could not control his men by law and became even more arrogant and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 鞭捶驛吏，貪求無已。

translations.literal: He whipped postal clerks and greedily demanded without end.
translations.idiomatic: He whipped postal clerks and made endless greedy demands.

sentences.zh: 載義因召李暢與語曰：「可汗使將軍朝貢，以固舅甥之好，不當使將軍暴踐中華。

translations.literal: Zaiyi therefore summoned Li Chang and spoke to him, saying: "The qaghan sent the general to pay court tribute in order to strengthen the bond of uncle and nephew; he should not have the general trample violently upon the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi summoned Li Chang and said to him, "The qaghan sent you to pay tribute and strengthen the bond between uncle and nephew. He did not send you to rampage through the Central Realm.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷饔餼至厚，所以禮蕃客也。

translations.literal: Now the court's provisions are extremely generous — that is how foreign guests are treated.
translations.idiomatic: The court now provides you with lavish hospitality — that is how foreign guests are to be treated.

sentences.zh: 茍有不至，吏當坐死。

translations.literal: If anything falls short, the officials should be punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: If anything is lacking, the officials responsible deserve death.

sentences.zh: 若將軍之部伍不戢，淩侮上國，剽掠廬舍，載義必殺為盜者。

translations.literal: If the general's troops are not restrained, insult the superior state, and plunder dwellings, Zaiyi will surely kill those who act as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: But if your men cannot keep discipline, insult this realm, and plunder people's homes, I will kill anyone who behaves like a bandit.

sentences.zh: 將軍勿以法令可輕而不戒勵之！」

translations.literal: General, do not think the laws can be treated lightly and fail to warn and restrain them!
translations.idiomatic: General, do not imagine that the law may be treated lightly — warn your men and keep them in order!

sentences.zh: 遂罷防守之兵，而使兩卒司其門。

translations.literal: He then dismissed the guarding troops and had only two soldiers keep watch at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed the guard troops and posted only two soldiers at their gate.

sentences.zh: 虜知其心為下，無敢犯令。

translations.literal: The barbarians knew his resolve would not yield, and none dared violate his orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs knew he would not back down, and none of them dared break his injunctions.

sentences.zh: 九年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty and was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 載義晚年驕恣，慘暴一方。

translations.literal: In his later years Zaiyi was arrogant and willful, cruel and violent over his region.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Zaiyi grew arrogant and tyrannical, ruling his region with cruel violence.

sentences.zh: 以楊志誠復為部下所逐，過太原，載義躬身毆擊，遂欲殺之，賴從事救解以免。

translations.literal: When Yang Zhicheng was again driven out by his subordinates and passed through Taiyuan, Zaiyi personally beat him and then tried to kill him; he escaped only because a staff officer intervened to save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Zhicheng was again ousted by his own men and passed through Taiyuan, Zaiyi personally assaulted him and tried to kill him; only the intervention of a staff officer saved Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 然而擅殺志誠之妻孥及將卒。

translations.literal: Nevertheless he killed Zhicheng's wife, children, and officers and soldiers on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, he arbitrarily executed Zhicheng's wife, children, and accompanying officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 朝廷錄其功，屈法不問。

translations.literal: The court recorded his merit and bent the law without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The court, weighing his past service, bent the law and did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 楊志誠楊志誠，為幽州後院副兵馬使，事李載義。

translations.literal: Yang Zhicheng — Yang Zhicheng was deputy commander of the rear guard in Youzhou and served Li Zaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhicheng served as deputy commander of the Youzhou rear guard under Li Zaiyi.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷賜載義德政碑文。

translations.literal: At that time the court granted Zaiyi a stele inscription praising his virtuous administration.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court had granted Zaiyi a stele commemorating his virtuous rule.

sentences.zh: 載義延中使擊鞠，志誠亦與焉，遂於鞠場叫呼謀亂。

translations.literal: Zaiyi invited the imperial envoy to play cuju; Zhicheng also took part, and then at the cuju field shouted and plotted mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi entertained the imperial envoy with a game of cuju, and Zhicheng joined in; at the playing field Zhicheng suddenly shouted and incited a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 載義奔於易州，志誠乃為本道馬步都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Zaiyi fled to Yizhou, and Zhicheng then became overall commander of cavalry and infantry in the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi fled to Yizhou, and Zhicheng made himself overall commander of the circuit's cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 文宗聞之驚，急召宰臣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong heard of it he was alarmed and urgently summoned the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was alarmed when he heard the news and urgently summoned his chancellors.

sentences.zh: 時牛僧孺先至，上謂曰：「幽州今日之事可奈何？」

translations.literal: At that time Niu Sengru arrived first; the emperor said to him: "What is to be done about today's affair in Youzhou?
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru arrived first, and the emperor asked him, "What can be done about what has happened in Youzhou today?

sentences.zh: 僧孺曰：「此不足煩聖慮，臣被召疾趨氣促，容臣稍緩息以對。」

translations.literal: Sengru said: "This is not worth troubling Your Majesty's concern. I was summoned in haste and am short of breath; allow me to catch my breath slightly before answering."
translations.idiomatic: Sengru replied, "This is not worth troubling Your Majesty. I was summoned in such haste that I am still breathless — allow me a moment to recover before I answer."

sentences.zh: 上良久曰：「卿以為不足憂，何也？」

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor said: "You think it is not worth worrying about — why?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the emperor said, "You say there is nothing to worry about — why?"

sentences.zh: 僧孺對曰：「陛下以范陽得失系國家休戚耶？

translations.literal: Sengru replied: "Does Your Majesty believe that the gain or loss of Fanyang is tied to the nation's weal and woe?
translations.idiomatic: Sengru answered, "Does Your Majesty believe the fate of Fanyang is bound up with the life and death of the state?

sentences.zh: 且自安、史之後，范陽非國家所有。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the time of An and Shi, Fanyang has not belonged to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Since the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellions, Fanyang has not truly belonged to the court.

sentences.zh: 前時劉總向化，以土地歸闕，朝廷約用錢八十萬貫，而未嘗得范陽尺布鬥粟上供天府；

translations.literal: Earlier when Liu Zong turned toward the court and returned his territory to the throne, the court agreed to spend eight hundred thousand strings of cash, yet never received from Fanyang even a foot of cloth or a peck of grain supplied to the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong submitted and returned his territory, the court agreed to pay eight hundred thousand strings of cash — yet Fanyang never sent so much as a foot of cloth or a peck of grain to the imperial storehouses.

sentences.zh: 則今日志誠之得，猶前日載義之得也。

translations.literal: Then Zhicheng's gaining power today is just like Zaiyi's gaining power the other day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng's rise today is no different from Zaiyi's rise yesterday.

sentences.zh: 陛下但因而撫之，亦事之宜也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only accordingly pacify him — that is also what the situation calls for.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need only accept the situation and conciliate him — that is the appropriate course.

sentences.zh: 且范陽，國家所賴者，以其北捍突厥，不令南寇。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the state relies on Fanyang for is that it holds off the Turks to the north and keeps them from raiding southward.
translations.idiomatic: What the court needs from Fanyang is for it to hold the northern frontier against the Turks and keep them from raiding south.

sentences.zh: 今若假志誠節鉞，惜其土地，必自為力。

translations.literal: If now we lend Zhicheng seals and credentials and value his territory, he will surely exert himself on his own.
translations.idiomatic: If we now grant Zhicheng the commission and leave his territory intact, he will surely exert himself on our behalf.

sentences.zh: 則爪牙之用，固不計於逆順。

translations.literal: Then the use of a claw and fang — loyalty or rebellion is naturally not the point.
translations.idiomatic: When one needs a fighting tool, one does not ask whether it has been loyal or rebellious.

sentences.zh: 臣固曰不足煩聖慮。」

translations.literal: I therefore say it is not worth troubling Your Majesty's concern."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I say this is not worth troubling Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上大喜曰：「如卿之言，吾洗然矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "As you say, I am completely relieved."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and said, "What you say clears my mind entirely."

sentences.zh: 尋以嘉王運遙領節度，以志誠為節度觀察留後，檢校左散騎常侍，兼幽州左司馬。

translations.literal: Soon Prince Yun of Jia was made titular military governor at a distance, and Zhicheng was made military governor and surveillance commissioner as acting administrator, acting Left Regular Attendant, and concurrently Left Assistant Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Prince Yun of Jia was named titular military governor, while Zhicheng was appointed acting administrator, surveillance commissioner, acting Left Regular Attendant, and Left Assistant Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋改檢校工部尚書、節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to acting Minister of Works, vice military governor, with charge of military governorship affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to acting Minister of Works and vice military governor with full control of circuit affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 詔下，進奏官徐迪詣中書白宰相曰：「軍中不識朝廷體位，只知自尚書改僕射為遷，何知工部轉吏部為美？

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, the memorial envoy Xu Di went to the Secretariat and told the chancellors: "The army does not understand court ranks; it only knows that changing from Minister to Vice Director is a promotion — how would it know that transferring from Works to Personnel is an honor?
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, the memorial envoy Xu Di went to the Secretariat and told the chancellors, "The soldiers do not understand court ranks. They know that going from minister to vice director counts as promotion — how would they see a move from Minister of Works to Minister of Personnel as an honor?

sentences.zh: 且軍士盛飾以待新恩，一旦復為尚書，軍中必慚。

translations.literal: Moreover the soldiers have dressed in finery awaiting the new favor; if they suddenly become ministers again, the army will surely be shamed.
translations.idiomatic: The troops have already dressed in their best, expecting a new honor. If they are suddenly made ministers again, the army will be humiliated.

sentences.zh: 今中使往彼，其勢恐不得出。」

translations.literal: If an imperial envoy goes there now, I fear he will not be able to leave.
translations.idiomatic: If an imperial envoy goes there now, I fear he may not be able to return.

sentences.zh: 及使至，其傔奔還，奏曰：「楊志誠怒不得僕射，三軍亦有怨言。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, his attendants fled back and reported: "Yang Zhicheng is angry at not receiving the vice directorship; the three armies also have complaints.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, his attendants fled back and reported, "Yang Zhicheng is furious at not receiving the vice directorship, and the whole army is muttering in discontent.

sentences.zh: 春衣使魏寶義、兼他使焦奉鸞，尹士恭，並為志誠縶留矣。」

translations.literal: The spring-clothing envoy Wei Baoyi, the envoy Jiao Fengluan, and Yin Shigong have all been detained by Zhicheng."
translations.idiomatic: The spring-clothing envoy Wei Baoyi, the envoy Jiao Fengluan, and Yin Shigong have all been detained by Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 志誠遣將王文穎謝恩，並讓官，復賜官告批答，文穎不受而歸。

translations.literal: Zhicheng sent the general Wang Wenying to express thanks and decline the office; the court again granted an appointment notice with a written reply, but Wenying refused it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng sent the general Wang Wenying to express thanks while declining the appointment; the court issued another commission with a written reply, but Wenying refused it and returned.

sentences.zh: 朝廷納裴度言，務以含垢，下詔諭之，因再遣使加尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: The court accepted Pei Du's advice, striving to swallow insults, issued an edict to instruct him, and again sent an envoy to add the post of Right Vice Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted Pei Du's counsel, resolved to swallow the insult, issued an edict of explanation, and sent another envoy to appoint Zhicheng Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 八年，為三軍所逐，則立史元忠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was driven out by the three armies, and Shi Yuanzhong was installed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the three armies drove him out and installed Shi Yuanzhong in his place.

sentences.zh: 元忠進志誠所造袞龍衣二副及被服鞍韉，皆繡飾鸞鳳日月之形，或為王字。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong presented two sets of dragon robes made by Zhicheng, along with clothing, saddles, and bridles, all embroidered with phoenixes, the sun and moon, or the character for "prince."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong presented two dragon robes Zhicheng had made, along with clothing, saddles, and bridles embroidered with phoenixes, the sun and moon, and even the character wang — "prince."

sentences.zh: 因付御史臺按問，流嶺南。

translations.literal: They were therefore handed to the Censorate for investigation, and he was banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Censorate for investigation, and Zhicheng was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 行至商州，殺之。

translations.literal: When he reached Shangzhou he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed when he reached Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，元忠既逐志誠，詔以通王淳遙領節度，授元忠左散騎常侍、幽州大都督府左司馬、知府事，充節度留後。

translations.literal: At first, after Yuanzhong had driven out Zhicheng, an edict made Prince Chun of Tong titular military governor at a distance, appointing Yuanzhong Left Regular Attendant, Left Assistant Governor of the Youzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, with charge of prefectural affairs, serving as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanzhong drove out Zhicheng, the court named Prince Chun of Tong titular military governor and appointed Yuanzhong Left Regular Attendant and Left Assistant Governor of Youzhou Metropolitan Prefecture with charge of its affairs, serving as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉檢校工部尚書、節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to acting Minister of Works, vice military governor, with charge of military governorship affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to acting Minister of Works and vice military governor with full control of circuit affairs.

sentences.zh: 後為偏將陳行泰所殺。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by the deputy general Chen Xingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He was later killed by the deputy general Chen Xingtai.

sentences.zh: 張仲武張仲武，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongwu — Zhang Zhongwu was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 仲武少業《左氏春秋》，擲筆為薊北雄武軍使。

translations.literal: Zhongwu in his youth studied the *Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals*, then cast aside his brush and became commissioner of the Xiongwu Army north of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu studied the Zuo Commentary in his youth, then put aside his brush and became commander of the Xiongwu Army north of Ji.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，陳行泰殺節度使史元忠，權主留後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huichang reign, Chen Xingtai killed the military governor Shi Yuanzhong and held the acting administrator's post on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huichang era Chen Xingtai killed the military governor Shi Yuanzhong and seized control as acting administrator.

sentences.zh: 俄而，行泰又為次將張絳所殺，令三軍上表，請降符節。

translations.literal: Before long Xingtai was also killed by the next-ranking general Zhang Jiang, who had the three armies submit a memorial requesting the bestowal of seals and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xingtai was killed in turn by the next-ranking general Zhang Jiang, who had the three armies petition the court for an official commission.

sentences.zh: 時仲武遣軍吏吳仲舒表請以本軍伐叛。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongwu sent the army clerk Wu Zhongshu with a memorial requesting that his own army be used to suppress the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu then sent his army clerk Wu Zhongshu with a memorial asking that his own troops be sent to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 上遣宰臣詢其事，仲舒曰：「絳與行泰，皆是遊客，主軍人心不附。

translations.literal: The emperor sent chancellors to inquire into the matter; Zhongshu said: "Jiang and Xingtai are both wandering adventurers; the army's hearts are not attached to them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent chancellors to inquire into the matter. Zhongshu said, "Jiang and Xingtai are both outsiders; the army has no real loyalty to either of them.

sentences.zh: 仲武是軍中舊將張光朝之子，年五十餘，兼曉儒書，老於戎事，性抱忠義，願歸心闕廷。」

translations.literal: Zhongwu is the son of the old army general Zhang Guangchao; he is over fifty years old, also versed in Confucian texts, long experienced in military affairs, by nature loyal and righteous, and wishes to give his heart to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu is the son of the veteran general Zhang Guangchao. He is over fifty, versed in the classics as well as in war, experienced in military affairs, and by nature loyal — he wishes to devote himself to the court.

sentences.zh: 李德裕因奏：「陳行泰、張絳皆令大將上奏，邀求節旄，所以必不可與。

translations.literal: Li Deyu thereupon memorialized: "Chen Xingtai and Zhang Jiang both had great generals submit memorials to demand seals and credentials — therefore they must on no account be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu then memorialized, "Both Chen Xingtai and Zhang Jiang had their generals petition the throne demanding commissions — for that reason they must on no account be granted.

sentences.zh: 今仲武上表布誠，先陳密款，因而拔用，即似有名。」

translations.literal: Now Zhongwu has submitted a memorial declaring his loyalty, first setting forth a secret pledge of allegiance; to promote him on that basis would seem justified."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu has now memorialized the throne with a pledge of loyalty, offering his allegiance in advance. To appoint him on that basis would seem legitimate."

sentences.zh: 許之，乃授兵馬留後，詔撫王纮遙領節度。

translations.literal: The request was granted; he was appointed acting commander of the army, and an edict made Prince Hong of Fu titular military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and appointed him acting army commander, while Prince Hong of Fu was named titular military governor by edict.

sentences.zh: 尋改仲武節度副大使、知節度事，檢校工部尚書、幽州大都督府長史、兼御史大夫、蘭陵郡王。

translations.literal: Soon Zhongwu was made vice military governor with charge of military governorship affairs, acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of the Youzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Prince of Lanling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu was soon made vice military governor with full control of circuit affairs, acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of Youzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Prince of Lanling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 俄而回鶻擾邊。

translations.literal: Before long the Uyghurs harassed the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Uyghurs began raiding the frontier.

sentences.zh: 時回鶻有將勒那頡啜擁赤心宰相一族七千帳，東逼漁陽。

translations.literal: At that time among the Uyghurs the general Lenan Juechuo led seven thousand tents of the Chixin chancellor's clan and pressed east toward Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Uyghur general Lenan Juechuo led seven thousand tents of the Chixin chancellor's clan east toward Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 仲武遣其弟仲至與裨將遊奉寰、王如清等，率銳兵三萬人大破之。

translations.literal: Zhongwu sent his younger brother Zhongzhi together with the deputy generals You Fenghuan, Wang Ruqing, and others to lead thirty thousand elite troops and inflict a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu sent his brother Zhongzhi with the deputy generals You Fenghuan and Wang Ruqing to lead thirty thousand crack troops and rout them.

sentences.zh: 前後收其侯王貴族千餘人，降三萬人，獲牛馬、橐駝、旗纛、罽幕不可勝計。

translations.literal: In all they captured more than a thousand of their princes and nobles, accepted the surrender of thirty thousand men, and seized cattle, horses, camels, banners, and felt tents beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: They captured more than a thousand Uyghur princes and nobles, accepted the surrender of thirty thousand men, and seized countless cattle, horses, camels, banners, and felt tents.

sentences.zh: 遣從事李周瞳、牙門將國從，相次獻捷。

translations.literal: He sent the staff officer Li Zhoutong and the gate officer Guo Cong in succession to present reports of victory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his staff officer Li Zhoutong and gate officer Guo Cong in turn to report the victories to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔加檢校兵部尚書，兼東面招撫回鶻使。

translations.literal: An edict added the acting post of Minister of War and made him commissioner for pacifying the Uyghurs on the eastern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The court promoted him to acting Minister of War and appointed him commissioner for pacifying the Uyghurs on the eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 先是，奚、契丹皆有回鶻監護使，督以歲貢，且為漢諜。

translations.literal: Earlier, both the Xi and the Khitan had Uyghur supervisory envoys who enforced the annual tribute and also served as spies for the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Previously both the Xi and the Khitan had Uyghur supervisory envoys who collected annual tribute and also acted as spies for the Tang.

sentences.zh: 至是，遣裨將石公緒等諭意兩部，凡戮八百餘人。

translations.literal: At this time he sent the deputy general Shi Gongxu and others to convey his intent to the two tribes; in all more than eight hundred were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent the deputy general Shi Gongxu and others to instruct the two tribes, and more than eight hundred Uyghur envoys were killed.

sentences.zh: 又回鶻初遣宣門將軍等四十七人，詭詞結歡，潛伺邊隙。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Uyghurs had first sent forty-seven men including the Xuanmen General with flattering words to win favor while secretly watching for openings on the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs had also sent forty-seven men, including the Xuanmen General, with smooth words of friendship while secretly probing for weaknesses on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 仲武使密賂其下，盡得陰謀。

translations.literal: Zhongwu had his men secretly bribe their subordinates and learned their entire plot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu secretly bribed their followers and learned their whole conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 且欲馳入五原，驅掠雜虜。

translations.literal: They also intended to ride into Wuyuan and drive off the various barbarian peoples in plunder.
translations.idiomatic: They also planned to ride into Wuyuan and plunder the various frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 遂逗遛其使，緩彼師期。

translations.literal: He therefore detained their envoys and delayed the date of their campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore detained their envoys and delayed the date of their planned raid.

sentences.zh: 人馬病死，竟不遣之。

translations.literal: Men and horses sickened and died, and in the end they were never sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Their men and horses sickened and died, and in the end they were never allowed to depart.

sentences.zh: 回鶻烏介可汗既敗，不敢近邊，乃依康居求活，盡徙餘種，寄托黑車子部。

translations.literal: After the Uyghur qaghan Wujie was defeated, he did not dare approach the border; he relied on Kangju to survive, moved all the remaining tribes, and entrusted himself to the Black Cart tribe.
translations.idiomatic: After the Uyghur qaghan Wujie was defeated, he dared not approach the border again. He sought refuge in Kangju, moved all his remaining people, and placed himself under the protection of the Black Cart tribe.

sentences.zh: 仲武由是威加北狄，表請於薊北立《紀聖功銘》，敕李德裕為之文，其銘曰：

translations.literal: Zhongwu thereby gained authority over the northern barbarians; he memorialized requesting that a "Record of Sacred Merit" stele be erected north of Ji, and an edict ordered Li Deyu to compose the text. The inscription reads:
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu's prestige over the northern peoples was now supreme. He memorialized asking that a 《Record of Sacred Merit》 stele be erected north of Ji, and the court ordered Li Deyu to compose the inscription, which reads:

sentences.zh: 仲武歷官至司徒、中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Zhongwu rose in office to Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu eventually reached the posts of Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 大中年卒，謚曰莊。

translations.literal: He died in the Dazhong reign and was given the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Dazhong era and was posthumously titled Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子 直方子直方，以幽州節度副使襲父位。

translations.literal: His son Zhifang — Zhifang — succeeded to his father's position as vice military governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhifang succeeded to his father's post as vice military governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 動多不法，慮為將卒所圖。

translations.literal: His actions were often unlawful, and he feared the officers and soldiers might plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was often lawless, and he feared his officers and soldiers might turn against him.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，托以遊獵，奔赴闕庭，尋授金吾將軍。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he pretended to go hunting, fled to the imperial court, and was soon appointed General of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he pretended to go hunting, fled to the capital, and was soon appointed General of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 直方性率暴，行豪奪之事，以罪累貶柳州司馬。

translations.literal: Zhifang was by nature reckless and violent and committed acts of forcible seizure; for repeated offenses he was demoted to defender of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang was reckless and violent by nature and committed acts of robbery and extortion; for repeated offenses he was demoted to defender of Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷右驍衛將軍，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard and assigned to the Eastern Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard with duty at the Eastern Capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，位至羽林統軍。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong reign he reached the post of commander of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era he rose to commander of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 中和歲，賊巢犯闕，公卿恃其豪，多隱藏於第。

translations.literal: In the Zhonghe years, when the rebel Huang Chao attacked the capital, the high officials relied on his boldness and many hid in his residence.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhonghe era, when Huang Chao's rebels stormed the capital, many high officials relied on Zhifang's boldness and took refuge in his mansion.

sentences.zh: 直方納招亡命，謀欲劫巢。

translations.literal: Zhifang gathered and recruited fugitives and plotted to seize Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang recruited fugitives and plotted to capture Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 或有告者，由是以兵圍而害之。

translations.literal: When someone reported this, Huang Chao therefore surrounded him with troops and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the plot leaked out, Huang Chao sent troops to surround and kill him.

sentences.zh: 張允伸張允伸，字逢昌，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yunshen — Zhang Yunshen, styled Fengchang, was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunshen, styled Fengchang, was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖秀，檀州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu was prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiu served as prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖巖，納降軍使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was commissioner of the Surrendered Armies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan served as commissioner of the Surrendered Armies.

sentences.zh: 父朝掖，贈太尉。

translations.literal: His father Chaoye was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chaoye was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 允申世仕幽州軍門，累職至押衙，兼馬步都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Yunshen's family for generations served in the Youzhou military establishment, rising through posts to commandant of the guard and overall commander of cavalry and infantry.
translations.idiomatic: For generations Yunshen's family served in the Youzhou army, and he rose through the ranks to commandant of the guard and overall commander of cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 大中四年，戎帥周綝寢疾，表允伸為留後，朝廷可其奏，加右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong the military commander Zhou Lin fell gravely ill and memorialized that Yunshen be made acting administrator; the court approved the memorial and added the post of Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong the military commander Zhou Lin fell gravely ill and recommended Yunshen as acting administrator. The court approved and appointed Yunshen Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，詔賜旌節，遷檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter an edict bestowed banners and credentials and transferred him to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the court bestowed banners and credentials on him and promoted him to acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: ，累加至光祿大夫、檢校司徒、兼太傅、同中書門下平章事、燕國公。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 十年，徐人作亂，請以弟允臯領兵伐叛，懿宗不允。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the people of Xu rebelled; he requested that his younger brother Yunguo lead troops to suppress the rebellion, but Emperor Yizong did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the people of Xu rebelled, Yunshen asked to send his younger brother Yunguo to lead troops against them, but Emperor Yizong refused.

sentences.zh: 進助軍米五十萬石，鹽二萬石。

translations.literal: He presented five hundred thousand shi of grain and twenty thousand shi of salt to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he contributed five hundred thousand shi of grain and twenty thousand shi of salt to support the campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉之，賜以錦彩、玉帶、金銀器等。

translations.literal: An edict commended him and bestowed brocade, a jade belt, gold and silver vessels, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his contribution and rewarded him with brocade, a jade belt, gold and silver vessels, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 冬，又加特進，兼侍中。

translations.literal: In winter he was further made specially advanced and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was further honored as specially advanced and appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以風恙拜章請就醫藥，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, on account of wind ailment he submitted a memorial requesting leave for medical treatment, and an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he submitted a memorial citing illness and asking leave for medical treatment, and the court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 以子簡會檢校工部尚書，充節度副大使。

translations.literal: His son Jianhui was made acting Minister of Works and vice military governor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jianhui was appointed acting Minister of Works and vice military governor.

sentences.zh: 十三年，允伸再上表進納所賜旌節。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Yunshen again submitted a memorial returning the banners and credentials he had been granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Yunshen again memorialized the throne, formally returning the banners and credentials he had been granted.

sentences.zh: 朝命未至，其年正月二十五日卒，年八十八。

translations.literal: Before the court's order arrived, on the twenty-fifth day of the first month of that year he died at the age of eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Before the court's reply arrived, he died on the twenty-fifth day of the first month of that year at the age of eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 再贈太尉，謚曰忠烈。

translations.literal: He was again posthumously made Grand Marshal and given the posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored again as Grand Marshal and given the posthumous title Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 允伸領鎮凡二十三年，克勤克儉，比歲豐登。

translations.literal: Yunshen held the command for twenty-three years in all, diligent and frugal; year after year the harvests were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Yunshen held command for twenty-three years, ruling with diligence and frugality, and harvests were abundant year after year.

sentences.zh: 邊鄙無虞，軍民用乂。

translations.literal: The frontier was untroubled, and the army and people lived in order.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was secure, and both army and people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 至今談者美之。

translations.literal: To this day those who speak of it praise him.
translations.idiomatic: People still speak of his rule with admiration.

sentences.zh: 有子十四人。

translations.literal: He had fourteen sons in all.
translations.idiomatic: He had fourteen sons.

sentences.zh: 簡真，幽府左司馬，先允伸卒。

translations.literal: Jianzhen was Left Assistant Governor of the Youzhou prefectural office and died before Yunshen.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhen served as Left Assistant Governor of Youzhou and died before his father.

sentences.zh: 簡壽，右領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Jianshou was great general of the Right Leading Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jianshou served as great general of the Right Leading Guard.

sentences.zh: 餘或升朝籍，或為刺史、郡佐。

translations.literal: The rest either entered the court registers or served as prefects and county aides.
translations.idiomatic: The others either entered court service or served as prefects and local officials.

sentences.zh: 張公素張公素，范陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongsu — Zhang Gongsu was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，為幽州軍校。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong reign he was a military officer in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era he served as a military officer in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 事張允伸，累遷至平州刺史。

translations.literal: He served Zhang Yunshen and was promoted cumulatively to prefect of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Zhang Yunshen and rose to prefect of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 允伸卒，子簡會權主留後事，公素領本郡兵赴焉。

translations.literal: When Yunshen died, his son Jianhui held the acting administrator's post on his own authority; Gongsu led the troops of his commandery to go there.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunshen died, his son Jianhui seized control as acting administrator, and Gongsu led the troops of his commandery to the capital of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 三軍素畏公素威望，簡會知力不能制，即時出奔，遂立為帥。

translations.literal: The three armies had long feared Gongsu's prestige; Jianhui knew he lacked the power to control the situation and fled at once, and Gongsu was thereupon installed as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies had long respected Gongsu's authority. Jianhui realized he could not control them and fled immediately, and the troops installed Gongsu as commander.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋授旌節，累加至中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The court soon bestowed banners and credentials and cumulatively promoted him to Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon invested him with banners and credentials and eventually promoted him to Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 無幾，李茂勛奪其位，公素歸闕，貶復州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Before long Li Maoxun seized his position; Gongsu returned to court and was demoted to registrar of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Maoxun seized his position. Gongsu returned to the capital and was demoted to registrar of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 李可舉李可舉，本回鶻阿布思之族也。

translations.literal: Li Keju — Li Keju was originally of the Uyghur Abusi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keju was originally of the Uyghur Abusi clan.

sentences.zh: 張仲武破回鶻，可舉父茂勛與本部侯王降焉。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhongwu defeated the Uyghurs, Keju's father Maoxun together with the princes and kings of their tribe surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhongwu defeated the Uyghurs, Keju's father Maoxun surrendered along with the princes and nobles of their tribe.

sentences.zh: 茂勛善騎射，性沈毅，仲武器之。

translations.literal: Maoxun was skilled at mounted archery and by nature steady and resolute; Zhongwu valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxun was skilled at mounted archery and steady by nature, and Zhongwu valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 常遣拓邊，以功封郡王，賜姓名。

translations.literal: He was often sent to expand the frontier; for merit he was enfeoffed as prince of a commandery and granted a surname and personal name.
translations.idiomatic: He was often sent on frontier campaigns, and for his achievements was enfeoffed as a commandery prince and granted a Chinese surname and personal name.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，納降軍使陳貢言者，幽之宿將，人所信服。

translations.literal: Late in the Xiantong reign, Chen Gongyan, commissioner of the Surrendered Armies, was an old general of Youzhou whom people trusted and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xiantong era Chen Gongyan, commissioner of the Surrendered Armies, was a veteran general of Youzhou whom the troops trusted and respected.

sentences.zh: 茂勛密謀劫而殺之，聲雲貢言舉兵。

translations.literal: Maoxun secretly plotted to seize and kill him, spreading word that Gongyan was raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxun secretly plotted to ambush and kill him, spreading the rumor that Gongyan was raising troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 張公素以兵逆擊不利，公素走，茂勛入城，軍民方知其非貢言也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongsu met him with troops in counterattack but fared badly; Gongsu fled, Maoxun entered the city, and only then did the army and people learn it had not been Gongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu marched out to oppose him but was defeated. Gongsu fled, Maoxun entered the city, and only then did the army and people realize the rebellion had not been Gongyan's doing.

sentences.zh: 既有其眾，遂推而立之，朝廷即降符節。

translations.literal: Having gained control of the troops, they thereupon pushed forward and installed him; the court immediately bestowed seals and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Once he controlled the army, the troops installed him as commander, and the court promptly invested him with seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 無幾，以疾告老，授右僕射致仕，表可舉自節度副使、幽州左司馬加右散騎常侍，為節度留後。

translations.literal: Before long, citing illness he requested retirement; he was made Right Vice Director and retired, and memorialized that Keju be promoted from vice military governor and Left Assistant Governor of Youzhou to Right Regular Attendant as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Maoxun retired citing illness, was appointed Right Vice Director, and recommended that Keju be promoted from vice military governor and Left Assistant Governor of Youzhou to Right Regular Attendant and acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 中和中，累官至檢校太尉。

translations.literal: During the Zhonghe reign he was cumulatively promoted to acting Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhonghe era he rose to acting Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。

translations.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。

translations.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.
translations.idiomatic: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.

sentences.zh: 時可舉遣將李全忠攻易州。

translations.literal: At that time Keju sent the general Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Keju then sent the general Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 有次將劉仁恭者，多權數；

translations.literal: Among the deputy generals was one Liu Rengong, full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Among the deputy generals was Liu Rengong, a man of many stratagems.

sentences.zh: 攻之彌月不下，乃穴地道以入。

translations.literal: They besieged it for a full month without taking it, then dug a tunnel to enter.
translations.idiomatic: After a month of siege the city still held, so they dug a tunnel to enter it.

sentences.zh: 其城既下，易州士卒稍驕。

translations.literal: Once the city had fallen, the soldiers of Yizhou grew somewhat arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, the Yan army grew somewhat overconfident.

sentences.zh: 王處存引輕軍三千，以羊皮蒙之，夜伏於城外，仍別於間道以騎士伺之。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun led three thousand light troops, covered them with sheepskins, and lay in ambush outside the city by night; he also posted cavalry on a side path to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun led three thousand light troops, covered them with sheepskins, and hid outside the city by night, while posting cavalry on a side road to watch for an opportunity.

sentences.zh: 燕軍望見，謂之群羊，爭趨焉。

translations.literal: When the Yan army saw them from afar, they took them for a flock of sheep and rushed to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan soldiers saw them from a distance, mistook them for a flock of sheep, and rushed to capture them.

sentences.zh: 處存乘其無部伍，一擊大敗之，尋復其城。

translations.literal: Chucun took advantage of their lack of formation, struck once and inflicted a great defeat, and soon recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun struck while they were disordered, routed them in a single blow, and soon recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 全忠遁歸，懼可舉罪之，收其餘眾，反攻幽州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong fled back, fearing Keju would punish him; he gathered his remaining troops and counterattacked Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong fled home, fearing Keju would punish him for the defeat. He gathered his remaining troops and turned against Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 可舉危急，收集其族，登樓自燔而死。

translations.literal: Keju was in dire straits; he gathered his clan, ascended a tower, and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Keju, trapped and desperate, gathered his family, climbed a tower, and burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 李全忠李全忠，范陽人。

translations.literal: Li Quanzhong — Li Quanzhong was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quanzhong was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 廣明中，為棣州司馬。

translations.literal: During the Guangming reign he was defender of Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangming era he served as defender of Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 有蘆生於室，一尺三節，心惡之。

translations.literal: Reeds sprouted in his room, one chi tall with three joints; he was troubled at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Reeds sprouted in his room, one foot tall with three joints, and the omen troubled him.

sentences.zh: 謂別駕張建曰：「吾室生蘆，無乃怪歟？」

translations.literal: He said to the vice prefect Zhang Jian: "Reeds have sprouted in my room — could this be an omen?
translations.idiomatic: He said to the vice prefect Zhang Jian, "Reeds have sprouted in my room — could this be an ill omen?

sentences.zh: 建曰：「蘆，茅類，得澤而滋，公家有茅土之慶，殆天意乎！

translations.literal: Jian said: "Reeds belong to the rush family; given moisture they flourish. Your lordship has the blessing of fief and soil — could this be Heaven's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "Reeds are a kind of rush; given water they flourish. Your lordship has the blessing of a fief — could this be Heaven's intent?

sentences.zh: 其生三節，必傳節鉞者三人。

translations.literal: That it sprouted with three joints means three men will in succession receive seals and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Three joints mean three generations will hold the commission of seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 公勉樹功名，無忘斯言。」

translations.literal: My lord, strive to build merit and fame, and do not forget these words."
translations.idiomatic: Strive to build your merit and fame, my lord, and do not forget these words."

sentences.zh: 全忠秩滿還鄉里，事節度使李可舉為牙將。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong's term expired he returned to his home district and served the military governor Li Keju as a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired Quanzhong returned home and served the military governor Li Keju as a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 時可舉兵鋒方盛，欲與鎮人分易、定，遣全忠將兵攻之，為定州軍大敗於易水。

translations.literal: At that time Keju's military power was at its height; wishing to divide Yi and Ding with the men of Zhen, he sent Quanzhong to lead troops in attack, but the army of Dingzhou inflicted a great defeat on them at the Yi River.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Keju's armies were at their peak. Seeking to divide Yizhou and Dingzhou with the forces of Zhenzhou, he sent Quanzhong to attack them, but the Dingzhou army routed his forces at the Yi River.

sentences.zh: 全忠懼，率其餘眾掩攻幽州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was afraid and led his remaining troops in a surprise attack on Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong, fearing punishment, turned his remaining troops against Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 可舉死。

translations.literal: Keju died.
translations.idiomatic: Keju died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 三軍推全忠為留後，朝廷因以節鉞授之，春也。

translations.literal: The three armies pushed Quanzhong forward as acting administrator, and the court thereupon invested him with seals and credentials — it was spring.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies installed Quanzhong as acting administrator, and the court invested him with the commission that spring.

sentences.zh: 全忠卒，子匡威自襲父位，稱留後。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong died, his son Kuangwei seized his father's position on his own authority and styled himself acting administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong died, his son Kuangwei seized his father's position and styled himself acting administrator.

sentences.zh: 匡威素稱豪爽，屬遇亂離，繕甲燕薊，有吞四海之志。

translations.literal: Kuangwei had long been known for bold generosity; encountering turmoil and separation, he readied armor in Yan and Ji and harbored the ambition to swallow the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei had long been known for boldness and generosity. In those years of chaos he armed his forces in Yan and Ji and harbored ambitions to dominate the realm.

sentences.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。

translations.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.

sentences.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

sentences.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。

translations.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.

sentences.zh: 時鎔童幼，求援於燕；

translations.literal: At that time Rong was still a child and sought aid from Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was still young and appealed to Yan for help.

sentences.zh: 匡威親率軍應之。

translations.literal: Kuangwei personally led an army to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei personally led an army to his aid.

sentences.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

sentences.zh: 匡威弟匡籌，妻張氏有國色。

translations.literal: Kuangwei's younger brother Kuangchou had a wife, Lady Zhang, of unrivaled beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei's younger brother Kuangchou had a wife, Lady Zhang, whose beauty was famed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 師將發，家人會別，匡威酒酣，留張氏報之。

translations.literal: As the army was about to depart, the family gathered for farewell; Kuangwei, deep in wine, detained Lady Zhang and violated her.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was about to march, the family gathered to say farewell. Kuangwei, drunk, detained Lady Zhang and violated her.

sentences.zh: 匡籌私懷忿怒，匡威軍至博野，匡籌乃據城自為節度。

translations.literal: Kuangchou privately harbored rage; when Kuangwei's army reached Boye, Kuangchou seized the city and made himself military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou nursed his anger in secret. When Kuangwei's army reached Boye, Kuangchou seized the city and declared himself military governor.

sentences.zh: 匡威部下聞之，亡歸者半。

translations.literal: When Kuangwei's subordinates heard of it, half fled back.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuangwei's troops heard the news, half of them deserted and returned home.

sentences.zh: 匡威退無歸路，將入覲京師。

translations.literal: Kuangwei retreated with no way back and intended to go to court in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei retreated with nowhere to go and prepared to travel to the capital to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 時匡威留於深州，遣判官李抱貞奉章以聞。

translations.literal: At that time Kuangwei remained at Shenzhou and sent the judge Li Baozhen with a memorial to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei remained at Shenzhou and sent his judge Li Baozhen with a memorial to inform the court.

sentences.zh: 屬京師大亂之後，聞匡威來朝，市人震恐，咸曰「金頭王來謀社稷」，士庶有亡竄山谷者。

translations.literal: This came after the great chaos in the capital; when people heard Kuangwei was coming to court, the townspeople were terrified and all said, "The Golden-Headed King comes to plot against the state," and officials and commoners fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: This came after the great upheaval in the capital. When word spread that Kuangwei was coming to court, the people of the city were terrified. "The Golden-Headed King is coming to seize the realm," they cried, and officials and commoners fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 匡威其實不行，欲圖鎮州，示無留意。

translations.literal: Kuangwei in fact did not go; he wished to seize Zhenzhou and showed no intention of proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei never actually went. He intended to seize Zhenzhou and made a show of having no further designs.

sentences.zh: 鎔以匡威再來援己，致其失師，遣使迎歸府第，父事之。

translations.literal: Rong, because Kuangwei had twice come to aid him and thereby caused the loss of his army, sent envoys to welcome him back to the mansion and treated him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kuangwei had twice come to his aid and twice cost him his army, Rong sent envoys to welcome him to his mansion and treated him with the deference due a father.

sentences.zh: 匡威為鎔城郛繕甲，指陳方略，視鎔如子。

translations.literal: Kuangwei fortified the walls and readied armor for Rong, laid out strategy, and regarded Rong as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei fortified Rong's walls, readied his armor, laid out strategy, and treated Rong as a son.

sentences.zh: 每陰謀驟施，以悅人心。

translations.literal: He constantly enacted sudden secret plots to win people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly carried out sudden secret maneuvers to win the people's favor.

sentences.zh: 鎮之三軍，素忠於王氏，惡其所為。

translations.literal: The three armies of Zhen had long been loyal to the Wang clan and hated what he was doing.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies of Zhenzhou had long been loyal to the Wang clan and despised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 會鎔過匡威第慰忌辰，匡威縞衣裹甲，伏兵劫鎔入牙城。

translations.literal: When Rong happened to visit Kuangwei's mansion to observe a mourning anniversary, Kuangwei wore hemp mourning garments over armor and with hidden troops seized Rong and carried him into the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong came to Kuangwei's mansion to observe a mourning anniversary, Kuangwei wore mourning garments over his armor and used hidden troops to seize Rong and carry him into the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 鎔兵逆戰，燔東偏門，軍士呼噪登屋，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: Rong's troops fought back, burned the east side gate, and soldiers shouting climbed onto the roofs; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's troops fought back, burned the eastern gate, and soldiers shouting climbed onto the rooftops as arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 鎔僕墨君和亂中扶鎔登屋免難，而斬匡威以徇。

translations.literal: Rong's servant Mo Junhe in the chaos helped Rong climb onto a roof and escape harm, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed the head.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos Rong's servant Mo Junhe helped him climb onto a roof to safety, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed his head.

sentences.zh: 是歲，匡籌出師攻鎮之樂壽、武強以報恥。

translations.literal: That year Kuangchou marched out to attack Leshou and Wuqiang in Zhen to avenge the disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: That year Kuangchou marched against Leshou and Wuqiang in Zhenzhou to avenge the humiliation.

sentences.zh: 匡威部曲劉仁恭歸於河東。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong, a follower of Kuangwei, went over to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong, formerly one of Kuangwei's officers, defected to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 冬，河東聽仁恭之謀，出師進討。

translations.literal: In winter Hedong heeded Rengong's plan and marched out to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Hedong adopted Rengong's plan and marched out to attack Yan.

sentences.zh: 二月，敗燕軍於居庸，匡籌挈其族遁去，將赴京師。

translations.literal: In the second month they defeated the Yan army at Juyong; Kuangchou fled with his clan and intended to go to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they routed the Yan army at Juyong. Kuangchou fled with his family, intending to go to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至景城，為滄州節度使盧彥威所殺，掠其輜車、妓妾。

translations.literal: When he reached Jingcheng he was killed by Lu Yanwei, military governor of Cangzhou, who plundered his baggage train and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingcheng he was killed by Lu Yanwei, military governor of Cangzhou, who seized his baggage train and concubines.

sentences.zh: 匡籌妻張氏產於路，不能進，劉仁恭獲之，獻於李克用，後立為夫人，嬖寵專房。

translations.literal: Kuangchou's wife Lady Zhang gave birth on the road and could not proceed; Liu Rengong captured her and presented her to Li Keyong, who later made her his primary wife and favored her exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou's wife Lady Zhang gave birth on the road and could go no farther. Liu Rengong captured her and presented her to Li Keyong, who later made her his primary wife and favored her above all others.

sentences.zh: 李氏父子三葉，十年而亡。

translations.literal: The Li father and son for three generations perished within ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The Li clan, father and son across three generations, was destroyed within ten years.

sentences.zh: 【贊】史臣曰：大都偶國，亂之本也。

translations.literal: 【Commentary】 The historian says: A great metropolis rivaling the state is the root of chaos.
translations.idiomatic: 【Commentary】 The historian writes: When a great city rivals the throne, rebellion is never far behind.

sentences.zh: 故古先哲王建國，公侯之封，不過千乘，所以強幹弱枝，防其悖慢。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity in establishing states granted marquis and duke fiefs of no more than a thousand chariots, thereby strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches to guard against insolence.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sage kings of antiquity, when founding their states, granted fiefs of no more than a thousand chariots — to strengthen the center and weaken the periphery and guard against rebellion.

sentences.zh: 彼幽州者，列九圍之一，地方千里而遙，其民剛強，厥田沃壤。

translations.literal: That Youzhou was one of the nine domains; its territory extended a thousand li into the distance, its people were sturdy and strong, and its fields were rich soil.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou was one of the nine domains of the realm. Its territory stretched a thousand li, its people were hardy and fierce, and its land was rich.

sentences.zh: 遠則慕田光、荊卿之義，近則染祿山、思明之風。

translations.literal: From afar they admired the righteousness of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent times they were infected with the spirit of Lushan and Siming.
translations.idiomatic: From afar they admired the loyalty of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent times they were infected with the rebellious spirit of An Lushan and Shi Siming.

sentences.zh: 二百餘年，自相崇樹，雖朝廷有時命帥，而土人多務逐君。

translations.literal: For more than two hundred years they constantly elevated one another; though the court sometimes appointed commanders, the local people mostly sought to oust their lords.
translations.idiomatic: For more than two hundred years they constantly elevated their own leaders. Though the court sometimes appointed commanders, the local people mostly worked to drive them out.

sentences.zh: 習苦忘非，尾大不掉，非一朝一夕之故也。

translations.literal: Accustomed to hardship they forgot wrongdoing; the tail grew too large to wag — this was not the work of a single morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: Hardened by hardship, they forgot restraint; the tail had grown too large to control. This did not happen overnight.

sentences.zh: 若李載義、張仲武、張允伸因利乘便，獲領旌旗，以仁守之，恭順朝旨，亦足多也。

translations.literal: If men such as Li Zaiyi, Zhang Zhongwu, and Zhang Yunshen seized the opportunity, obtained command of the banners, ruled with benevolence, and respectfully followed court directives, that too was praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: When men such as Li Zaiyi, Zhang Zhongwu, and Zhang Yunshen seized their opportunity, won command of the banners, ruled with benevolence, and obeyed the court, they too deserve praise.

sentences.zh: 如硃克融、楊志誠、史元忠、張公素、李可舉、李全忠，以不仁得之，靡更曩志。

translations.literal: Men such as Zhu Kerong, Yang Zhicheng, Shi Yuanzhong, Zhang Gongsu, Li Keju, and Li Quanzhong obtained power through lack of benevolence and never changed their former ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Zhu Kerong, Yang Zhicheng, Shi Yuanzhong, Zhang Gongsu, Li Keju, and Li Quanzhong seized power through violence and never abandoned their old ambitions.

sentences.zh: 或尋為篡奪，或僅傳子孫，咸非令終，蓋其宜也。

translations.literal: Some were soon usurped, some passed power only to their descendants — none met good ends; that was only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Some were soon overthrown, others held power only long enough to pass it to their sons — none came to a good end, and that was only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：蠍石之野，氣勁人豪。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the wilds of Xieshi, the spirit is fierce and the men are bold.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary reads: In the wild country around Xieshi, the air is fierce and the men are bold.

sentences.zh: 二百餘載，自相尊高。

translations.literal: For more than two hundred years they elevated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: For more than two hundred years they raised themselves above the throne.

sentences.zh: 載義、仲武，亦多忠勞。

translations.literal: Zaiyi and Zhongwu also rendered much loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi and Zhongwu, too, served the court with notable loyalty.

sentences.zh: 餘因篡得，不仁何逃？

translations.literal: The rest obtained power through usurpation — how could lack of benevolence escape its due?
translations.idiomatic: The rest seized power by force — how could cruelty not bring its reckoning?
